_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.lead: You've dodged them a thousand times.
beats.text: They were never chasing you at random.
beats.note: Each of the four ghosts runs its own fixed formula for picking a target tile, results Namco's own team called their "personalities".

beats.text: Pinky isn't chasing you. He's ambushing you.
beats.note: His target sits four tiles ahead of wherever you're currently facing, so he tries to cut off your path instead of following it.

beats.text: Face upward, and the maths breaks.
beats.note: A logic error in the original code adds a phantom four-tile offset to the left as well, so "four tiles up" becomes four up and four left. It shipped in 1980 and stayed.

beats.name: Shigeo Funaki
beats.role: The programmer Namco paired with designer Toru Iwatani, who had no formal coding background himself. Between them they built four different hunting formulas, not four costumes on one script.

beats.context: Clyde's actual personal-space rule. Closer than this and he panics back to his corner; farther and he hunts you exactly like the red ghost.

beats.line: Four formulas. It only ever looked like a mind.
